content: Melvin-Koushki says Ibn Turka also manifests a paradoxical preference for earlier authorities in certain fields: in his manual of logic, the K. al-Manāhij, he rejects certain developments in post-Avicennan Arabic logic as breaking unduly with the teachings of the ancients; he wrote it in 833/1430 in Natanz for his son Jamāl al-Dīn Muḥammad.
